title: Hard Times, Together
description:
Another hard day.

Daeun came in and sat down beside {name} without asking anything.

"How was today?"

Those few words brought back the day {name} first said it out loud.
"Honestly, things have been really hard lately."

choices.text: "Still hard. But better with you here."
choices.result_text:
Daeun laughed a little, then said nothing.
She just stayed beside {name}.

"I want to go through the hard part with you." {name} didn't bring up what she had said that day. Her shoulder was there again today.

She looked skeptical. Didn't push.

Better or just numb — she probably couldn't tell.
Neither could {name}, honestly.

title: The Feed
description:
Months later.

The photo still surfaces sometimes. The wedding dress. The bright smile.

{name} does not resent her. It is simply strange that the smile now belongs to a life outside your memories.

Will a day come when you can smile like that too?

choices.result_text:
{name} had kept asking whether it was sincere. Today it seemed to be.

Different destinations. She reached hers.
{name} is still moving toward theirs.

Did it. No like, no comment.

She's living her life. {name} is living theirs.
Just a pause. Then keep going.

title: The Café Promise
description:
Daeun finished her first day at the Gangnam office.

'How was it?' {name} asked.
'Everyone walks so fast there.' She laughed.

You remembered the map pin you had saved. 'When you're in Gangnam, let's go to that café nearby.'

choices.result_text:
Gangnam café. Dae-un looked out the window.
'I can't believe I work here now.'

{name} was still on the outside of this neighborhood.
But at least he was sitting here today with coffee. A first.

choices.text: "I'll be there soon. Then we'll go."
choices.result_text:
'I know,' she said.

The promise still stands.
The day {name} walks through that neighborhood as a resident rather than a visitor — then the café.

title: Good, Said Dad
description:
Sunday evening call.

Dad brought it up.
'That man was in the news. The one you called me about.'

{name} paused.

choices.text: "Yes. But I learned things from him."
choices.result_text:
Dad thought about it, then:
'Even a flawed person teaches something.'

An unexpected kind of comfort.
That night, {name} still kept the books the way Sangchul had taught.

'Right,' Dad said. Moved on.

It was in the past. Im Sangchul had become a name in the newspaper.
{name} closed the article without reading to the end.

title: Two Things at Once
description:
Without him, {name} might not be here.
Because of him, Dad suffered for years.

Both are true at the same time.

Today that came back without warning.

choices.text: Accept both — that's the most honest framing
choices.result_text:
Someone you can neither repay nor resent.
{name} neither deleted Sangchul's number nor kept it in favorites.

choices.text: Still not resolved — more time needed
choices.result_text:
Not resolved. His name still catches at something.

Being unresolved isn't weak. It's not pretending.
When resolution comes, it'll come.

title: Finding It
description:
Message from Ji-yeon.

'Remember how we both said we were still figuring out our own way? I think I found mine.'

{name} recalled the alley. That conversation about paths.

choices.result_text:
Ji-yeon sent a small emoji.

Not deep friends, but people who knew they were headed the same way.

'That's still figuring it out,' Ji-yeon replied.

It didn't sound like comfort, but it wasn't wrong either.
{name} smiled a little and put the phone down.
